theme: 多 Agent 系統怎麼分工、抓錯與被監督
notes: Announcement batch confirmed via arxiv.org/list/{cat}/new page headers: Monday, 31 August 2026 (IDs prefixed 2608.27xxx-2608.28xxx). Groundlane web_search returned very few same-day candidates because papers this fresh are not yet indexed by external providers, so metadata for the full new-submission ID lists (cs.AI 94 + cs.CL 58 + cs.MA cross-list 10) was pulled directly from the arXiv export API (id_list batches) and titles screened for topical relevance.

An earlier draft selection (OBPE / CURA / EvoUndo, an agent-governance and runtime-safety cluster) was replaced before writing: the 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-30 digests already covered adjacent runtime-authorization/action-gating themes (AID-Guard stateful authorization; SARA action-induction vs runtime authorization; LoopHarness non-decaying loop state), so a fourth consecutive authorization-boundary theme in six days would have had lower incremental today-importance for readers despite each paper's individual credibility. The multi-agent collaboration/failure-attribution/observability cluster below had not been covered in the preceding week and was judged higher editorial value.
Full method, experiment, baseline, and limitation sections were read (not abstract-only) for all three selected papers via arxiv.org/html full text.

GOD is an EMNLP 2026 System Demonstrations Track paper; its own Limitations section states it tested one model configuration with repeated synthetic profiles and did not evaluate operator usability. It is selected as conditional-pass because it discloses this scope explicitly and is fully open-sourced, not because its evaluation is broad.

candidates.title: When Evidence Shapes Collaboration: Knowledge-Conditioned Topology Generation for Multi-Agent Systems
credibilityEvidence: Section 4: 7 benchmarks (MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GPQA, StrategyQA, GSM8K, AQuA, HumanEval) against 3 baseline categories (single large models, static topologies, dynamic MAS frameworks including LLM-Debate/AgentPrune/AgentDropout/AFlow/G-Designer).
Table 2 ablation: GPQA accuracy 38.48% (no KG) -> 49.26-50.00% (KG at inference) -> 50.75% (KG + verifier), isolating each component's contribution.

Table 3 knowledge-dependence analysis: closed-book vs open-book gains of +15.35% (MMLU-Pro) and +10.56% (GPQA), larger than single-agent and query-conditioned G-Designer baselines, supporting that gains come from evidence use rather than memorization.

Explicit Limitations section: depends on external KG quality/coverage, bounded topology size (N_max=6) limits long-horizon scalability, not yet extended to broader tool-use or dynamically evolving knowledge sources.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Multiple benchmark families, three baseline categories, component ablation, and a closed/open-book control together isolate the evidence-conditioning claim; the paper itself scopes generalization to knowledge-intensive QA rather than broader tool-use agents.
reproducibilityEvidence: Full method formalization, training/curriculum procedure, and per-dataset agent-role prompts given in the paper and appendix
No GitHub/code release or checkpoint link found in the fetched full text
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The reported +15.7pp GPQA gain and token-efficiency claim are supported by matched baselines and ablations; the paper does not overclaim beyond knowledge-intensive reasoning tasks.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Depends on a pre-built external knowledge graph (Wikipedia + StructSense pipeline) and a bounded topology size; not yet validated on long-horizon or live tool-use tasks.
candidates.presentationReason: Method, training objective, baselines, ablations, and a dedicated Limitations section are all explicit and separable.
candidates.reason: Reframes dynamic MAS topology generation from query-semantics-first to evidence-first, with the strongest same-batch quantitative result (GPQA +15.7pp at <half the tokens) and full ablation support.

candidates.title: Finding Where the Buck Stops: An Automated Failure Attribution-Based Reflection Framework for Multi-Agent Collaboration
credibilityEvidence: Section 4: DoCtOR improves initial success rate by 22%/26%/27% on HotPotQA/ChartQAPro/Mind2Web, outperforming named baselines Reflexion, Retroformer, and COPPER.
ProFA diagnosis submodule evaluated separately on the Who & When dataset: +4-35pp agent-level accuracy and +9-28pp step-level accuracy over existing attribution methods.
Generalization check: the diagnose-then-correct paradigm is shown to improve an existing prompt-based method (Reflexion) when grafted on, not only DoCtOR's own pipeline.
Accepted to EMNLP 2026 main conference track.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Three task datasets, three named baselines, a separately validated attribution submodule, and a cross-method generalization test together support the core 'reflect only the decisive-error agent' claim.
reproducibilityEvidence: Detailed prompts for action and reflection modules given in Appendix E
No independent public code repository confirmed in the fetched full text
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Consistent double-digit gains across three distinct task types (QA, chart understanding, web navigation) with matched baselines support the scoped claim about attribution-targeted reflection.
candidates.primaryLimitation: The ProFA diagnosis submodule itself requires a dataset with labeled decisive-error steps (Who & When Pro) for training; transfer of diagnostic accuracy to entirely new task domains is not evaluated.
candidates.presentationReason: Method decomposition (diagnosis / correction / targeted reflection), formalization, and experiment results are clearly separated and each tied to a specific ablation or dataset.
candidates.reason: Identifies and fixes a concrete failure mode in existing MAS self-reflection (forced reflection contaminating regular-behaving agents' memory) with cross-dataset evidence and a generalization test onto an existing baseline method.

candidates.title: GOD: Govern, Observe, and Direct - A Real-Time Control Room for Agent Societies
credibilityEvidence: Section 5: 15 completed run slots (1 baseline + 14 intervention runs from 10 scenario templates, 4 repeated); 78/84 target-destination checks and 169/182 state-answer checks matched replay records.

Section 5.3 discloses a mid-evaluation bug fix (Chinese-language command-parser routing collision) and explicitly labels the resulting 14/14 routing figure as a post-fix regression check, not a held-out generalization estimate.
Author-stated Limitations: one model configuration (Qwen-Plus) tested, repeated synthetic profiles across scenarios (not independent samples), no operator-usability study.
Fully open-sourced under Apache-2.0 with a public repository, hosted no-credential replays, and downloadable experiment/map/agent packs.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: This is an EMNLP System Demonstrations Track paper evaluating a command-to-artifact integration path, not agent intelligence or social validity; the author's own framing and Limitations section describe it as a small-scale demo evaluation.
reproducibilityEvidence: Hosted read-only replays requiring no credentials
Downloadable experiment, map, and agent packs
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: High confidence that operator commands are recorded and traceable against replay state within the tested scope; no confidence claim is made (by the paper or this review) about agent behavioral quality or operator usability.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Single model configuration and repeated synthetic profiles (not independent samples); no human operator usability evaluation.
candidates.presentationReason: The paper is unusually explicit about what its own metrics do and do not establish (e.g. distinguishing a causal effect from an agent already being at a location), including disclosing a mid-study bug and its remediation.
candidates.reason: Fills the observability/intervention angle of the day's theme (K-GAT=method, DoCtOR=failure evaluation, GOD=tooling/application) with an unusually transparent demo paper; included as conditional-pass with explicitly softened editorial language per its own disclosed scope.

candidates.title: CURA: Certified Runtime Alarms for Computer-Use Agents
credibilityEvidence: 361 OSWorld tasks, CUSUM sequential test with Learn-then-Test finite-sample false-alarm control, AUROC/recall reported with confidence intervals, honest that composite margin over token-count baseline is not significant (p=0.101).
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Rigorous statistics but single benchmark/environment (OSWorld computer-use tasks).
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Claims are tightly scoped to the tested pipeline and benchmark.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Single-benchmark generalization untested; retrospective composite not significantly better than a token-count baseline.
candidates.reason: Strong candidate for a runtime-safety/governance themed digest, but held back today to avoid a fourth consecutive authorization/runtime-safety theme in six days (see notes); revisit if the topic recurs with new angles.

candidates.title: If Agents Were Angels, No Governance Would Be Necessary: Out-of-Band Policy Enforcement at a Trusted Tool Boundary
credibilityEvidence: Formal order-independence/monotonicity proofs for policy composition; 3,621 trials across 4 models and 20 adaptive red-team tasks; trace-failure rate 57.6%->0.2% with 95% CI [27.7,54.9]pp reduction; explicit scope limits (no write controls, no durable approval, no temporal/aggregate policy).
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Formal proofs plus large multi-model red-team evaluation with confidence intervals and disclosed residual failure modes.
reproducibilityEvidence: Released simplified HTTP proxy prototype with Cedar conformance tests
candidates.primaryLimitation: Scope excludes write controls, durable approval, and temporal/aggregate policies; some exact values were reconstructed without entering context.
candidates.reason: Same reasoning as 2608.27808: strong pass, held for a future digest to avoid thematic repetition with 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-30 authorization/governance coverage.

candidates.title: EvoUndo: Recoverability-Constrained Self-Evolution for LLM Agent Harnesses
credibilityEvidence: 600 unseen self-evolution tasks, 2x2 grounding-by-expressivity factorial, cross-model replication (gpt-oss-120b vs Qwen3.8-27B) showing a model-dependent interaction, honestly reported rather than smoothed over.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Novel problem framing tested on constructed self-evolution tasks rather than deployed production harnesses.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Constructed benchmark of self-evolution tasks; cross-model interaction effect does not replicate consistently.
candidates.reason: Same reasoning as above: held back for thematic diversity; also the narrowest practical link of the three governance candidates today.
